concepts.title: Geometric Constructions with Instruments
concepts.definition: Precise figures are built with ruler, compass and set square: arcs copy lengths, perpendiculars make right angles, and each step follows from a property, so the finished figure carries its own proof.
concepts.key_idea: Construction is reasoning made visible: every arc is an argument drawn in pencil.

copy an angle using ruler and compass

concepts.title: Tilings: Shapes that Cover the Floor
concepts.definition: A tiling covers a surface with no gaps and no overlaps; some shapes tile beautifully, squares and equilateral triangles and regular hexagons fit around every point, while the regular pentagon famously refuses.
concepts.key_idea: Tiling is angle arithmetic at every point: the angles meeting at a corner must total a full 360 degrees.

concepts.title: Angles and Parallel Lines in Constructions
concepts.definition: Constructions lean on angle facts: copying an angle preserves its size, constructing a parallel line uses equal corresponding angles, and checking a drawn figure means re-measuring the angles the construction promised.
concepts.key_idea: Equal angles travel along constructions: copying and parallels both depend on keeping an angle exactly.

concepts.title: Checking Constructions by Properties
concepts.definition: A construction is finished only when its properties are verified: sides measured, corners tested for right angles, parallelism checked with a set square, because instruments drift and properties do not.
concepts.key_idea: Properties are the examiner: measure the finished figure against the definition before calling it done.
